data.narrative:
Atom Bodies is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Tyler Hayes, Doug Satzger, and Eric Monsef that has raised $142.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage companies including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of the three triangulation methods considered, only Stage-Progression valuation proved applicable. This method uses the company's $142.2M in total raised as a baseline value proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression in biotech, yielding an implied valuation of $284M. Peer-Median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient comparable peers meeting narrow same-stage and similar-tier filters—only 1 adjacent-stage peer was identified versus the minimum 3 required. Public-Comp Anchoring using the sector's 8.1x P/S median across the three public tickers could not be applied because the target's revenue is not on file, as is standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $242M to $327M, centered on $284M. This single-method result introduces material uncertainty. The range assumes typical biotech stage progression dynamics hold for this company. Key open questions include the company's revenue trajectory, clinical/product validation status, and how peer selection might shift if additional narrow-filter comparables become available.
